title: Languages you speak
goal: Say which languages you speak and how well, using the regular -er verb pattern.

drills.explain: ils → -ent: étudi + ent. The -ent is silent.
tu → -es, even though you can't hear the -s.

items.note: You will also see [[l'hindi]]; [[le hindi]] is the more standard form.

accept: Je parle un peu le français.

blocks.title: At a job fair in Ottawa
blocks.context: Amira talks to Alex, a recruiter at a bank stand.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.en: Hello, ma'am! Do you speak English?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Oui, je parle anglais et arabe. Et je parle un peu français.
lines.en: Yes, I speak English and Arabic. And I speak a little French.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.fr: Un peu ? Vous parlez bien français !
lines.en: A little? You speak French well!

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Merci ! J'étudie le français à Gatineau.
lines.en: Thank you! I'm studying French in Gatineau.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.fr: Ici, nous parlons français et anglais avec les clients.
lines.en: Here, we speak French and English with the customers.

blocks.title: Later, at the coffee stand
blocks.context: Raj and Mei, two job seekers, chat.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Non, je parle mandarin et anglais. Et toi ?
lines.en: No, I speak Mandarin and English. And you?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Je parle hindi, pendjabi et anglais. À la maison, nous parlons pendjabi.
lines.en: I speak Hindi, Punjabi and English. At home, we speak Punjabi.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.en: And do you speak French fluently?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Pas encore ! J'étudie le français, comme toi.
lines.en: Not yet! I'm studying French, like you.

blocks.body: Listen first. Notice the different endings: [[je parle]], [[tu parles]], [[nous parlons]], [[vous parlez]].

blocks.title: One pattern, thousands of verbs
blocks.body:
Most French verbs end in **-er**: [[parler]], [[étudier]], [[aimer]], and [[habiter]] from the last lesson. They all work the same way:

- remove **-er** → [[parl-]]
- add the ending for each person: **-e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent**

Learn this once and you can use almost every -er verb you meet.

blocks.title: Parler in the present
head: parler
English
rows: you speak (formal, or more than one person)
blocks.note: Four forms sound exactly the same: [[parle, parles, parle, parlent]] = *PARL*. Only [[parlons]] (*par-LON*) and [[parlez]] (*par-LÉ*) sound different.

blocks.title: Étudier and aimer: same endings
head: étudier
aimer
blocks.note: These verbs start with a vowel, so [[je]] becomes [[j']]: [[j'étudie]], [[j'aime]]. You also hear a *z* liaison: [[nous‿étudions]], [[vous‿aimez]], [[ils‿aiment]].

blocks.title: Parler + a language
blocks.pattern: parler + language (usually no article) · étudier / aimer + le / l' + language
blocks.note: Language names are **masculine** and take **no capital letter**. After [[parler]], people usually drop the article. After [[étudier]] and [[aimer]], keep it.

blocks.title: How well?
head: French
English
blocks.note: [[Un peu]], [[bien]] and [[très bien]] usually go **right after the verb**. [[Couramment]] often goes at the end. If you put it right after the verb, keep the article: [[Je parle couramment l'anglais.]]

blocks.title: Language or nationality?
blocks.body:
Many language names are the same word as the **masculine** nationality: [[français]], [[anglais]], [[espagnol]], [[arabe]]. Context tells you which one:

- [[Il est français.]] = He is French (nationality, with être).
- [[Il parle français.]] = He speaks French (the language, with parler).

For Chinese, [[le chinois]] is the general word; [[le mandarin]] is more precise. For Hindi, you'll see both [[le hindi]] (more standard) and [[l'hindi]]. Punjabi is also spelled [[le panjabi]].

- **Capital letters:** [[Je parle Anglais]] is wrong in French. Write [[Je parle anglais]].
- **le + vowel:** [[le anglais]] → [[l'anglais]], [[le espagnol]] → [[l'espagnol]].
- **être + verb:** English “I am speaking” is just [[je parle]] in French. Never [[je suis parle]].
- **Pronouncing -ent:** in [[ils parlent]], the -ent is silent. Say *il PARL*, not *il par-LENT*.

Canada has two official languages, [[le français]] and [[l'anglais]]. In job ads, [[bilingue]] almost always means **French and English**. In Québec, French is the official language of the province, so it is the normal language of work and public services.

After English and French, languages like Punjabi, Mandarin, Arabic and Spanish are among the most common in Canada, so you'll often hear [[Tu parles pendjabi ?]] or [[Vous parlez arabe ?]]

In informal Québec speech you may hear [[Tu parles-tu français ?]] The second [[tu]] just marks a yes/no question. It is very casual: understand it, but don't copy it yet.

examples.fr: Je suis bilingue : je parle français et anglais.
examples.en: I'm bilingual: I speak French and English.

blocks.title: Preview: saying you don't speak a language
blocks.body: You'll learn negation later. For now, you can use this as a chunk, like [[je ne comprends pas]] from unit 1: put [[ne]] before the verb and [[pas]] after it.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Say each line out loud, then record yourself and compare.

lines.tip: parlez ends in an é sound: par-LÉ. Let your voice rise at the end to make it a question.
The z sound in il-z‿aiment shows it's plural.

blocks.explain: You hear a *z* in [[elles‿aiment]], so it's plural. [[Elle aime]] has no z.

blocks.prompt: How do you say “I speak Spanish”?
optionFeedback: Language names take no capital letter in French.
Don't add être: “I speak” is just je parle.
le + a vowel becomes l', and with parler you usually drop the article anyway.

blocks.explain: Formal → [[vous parlez]]. Rising intonation is enough to make it a question.

accept: Je parle un peu le français.
blocks.hint: un peu goes right after the verb.
blocks.explain: [[Je parle un peu français.]] [[Un peu]] comes straight after [[parle]].
elle → [[parle]]. [[Couramment]] can go right after the verb or at the end.
[[étudiez]] starts with é and ends in -ez; [[l'espagnol]] has an apostrophe.

accept: Je m'appelle Mei, je suis chinoise et je parle mandarin.
Je m'appelle Mei. Je suis chinoise et je parle mandarin.
Je m'appelle Mei, je suis chinoise et je parle le mandarin.
Je m'appelle Mei. Je suis chinoise et je parle le mandarin.
Moi, c'est Mei, je suis chinoise et je parle mandarin.
Moi, c'est Mei, je suis chinoise et je parle le mandarin.
blocks.explain: Three verbs: [[je m'appelle]], [[je suis]] (+ feminine [[chinoise]]) and [[je parle]].

blocks.en: Do you like French? (to a friend)

blocks.prompt: A recruiter asks about your languages. Say which languages you speak and how well, say what you are studying, and ask the recruiter one question with vous.
checklist: How well: un peu / bien / couramment

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Je parle espagnol et anglais. Je parle anglais couramment, et je parle un peu français. J'étudie le français à Montréal. Et vous, vous parlez espagnol ?
models.en: I speak Spanish and English. I speak English fluently, and I speak a little French. I'm studying French in Montréal. And you, do you speak Spanish?

blocks.prompt: Fill in the “Languages” section of your profile on a volunteer website. Write 3 or 4 sentences about the languages you speak, study or like.
checklist: Je parle… with at least two languages
Say how well (un peu, bien, couramment)
Use j'étudie or j'aime with le / l'
No capital letters on language names

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Je parle hindi et pendjabi. Je parle très bien anglais. J'étudie le français et je parle un peu français. J'aime aussi l'espagnol !
models.en: I speak Hindi and Punjabi. I speak English very well. I'm studying French and I speak a little French. I like Spanish too!

summary:
- Conjugate regular **-er verbs**: [[je parle, tu parles, il/elle parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils/elles parlent]]
- Say which languages you speak: [[Je parle anglais et un peu français.]]
- Use [[j'étudie le français]] and [[j'aime l'espagnol]], with the article
- Ask [[Vous parlez anglais ?]] / [[Tu parles arabe ?]]
